chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Abu Baseer, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He is questioned while he is squeezed.'

key_terms.مَضْغُوطٌ: Squeezed or constricted (referring to the narrowing of the grave)
key_terms.يُسْأَلُ: He is questioned (referring to the interrogation in the grave)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person in the grave during the questioning according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise narration from al-Kafi highlights the physical torment of the grave (darb al-qabr) as the immediate context for the questioning by Munkar and Nakir. In Shia scholarship, this 'squeezing' is often interpreted not merely as physical constriction but as a manifestation of spiritual anxiety and the weight of one's deeds, serving as a precursor to the final judgment. It underscores the belief that the grave is a real, intermediate realm (barzakh) where the soul experiences tangible consequences of earthly actions.
